Yasmin El-Amin

Email: yasmin.elamin@email.com | Phone: (555) 123-4567 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/yasminelamin | GitHub: github.com/yasminelamin  

Professional Experience  
At VerveCorp, I focused on scalable backend systems, contributing to microservices architecture and automation workflows. As a Junior Backend Engineer, I developed REST APIs for enterprise SaaS platforms, reducing average query latency by 30% through PostgreSQL optimization. My work on CI/CD pipelines for Dockerized applications improved deployment reliability by 25%, enabling faster iteration cycles. As a Backend Engineer, I architected serverless functions on AWS, integrating Redis caching layers that reduced database load by 40% during peak traffic. These efforts supported high-availability applications with sub-100ms response times.  

During my internship at NexGen Technologies, I collaborated on building REST APIs for a SaaS platform, refining query performance by 22% through index optimization and query restructuring. This experience solidified my understanding of database indexing strategies and their impact on system scalability.  

Education  
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, University of Toronto (2022). Graduated with a focus on distributed systems and cloud computing, leveraging academic resources to deepen expertise in backend development and infrastructure automation.  

Technical Skills  
Docker and Kubernetes were central to deploying microservices at VerveCorp, where I managed container orchestration for applications handling over 10,000 requests per second. GitHub Actions automated testing and deployment workflows, ensuring 99.9% uptime for critical services. PostgreSQL optimization, including query indexing and connection pooling, reduced latency in high-traffic scenarios. Redis caching layers, implemented for session management, cut database load by 40%. Serverless functions on AWS enabled cost-effective scaling, with cloud cost optimization practices reducing monthly expenses by 15%. CI/CD pipelines, built using GitLab and Jenkins, streamlined release processes, cutting deployment time from hours to minutes. Infrastructure as Code tools like Terraform managed cloud resources, ensuring consistent environments across development and production. Monitoring tools such as Prometheus and Grafana provided real-time visibility into system performance, with alerts configured for critical thresholds.  

Projects  
Designed a serverless architecture for a real-time analytics dashboard, using AWS Lambda and API Gateway to process and visualize data from multiple sources. This project reduced infrastructure costs by 20% while maintaining low-latency response times.  

Publications  
Co-authored a technical blog post on optimizing PostgreSQL for microservices, published on VerveCorp’s engineering portal, which received over 5,000 views and sparked discussions on indexing strategies.  

Awards & Achievements  
Recognized as VerveCorp’s “Rising Star” in 2023 for contributions to cloud cost optimization and infrastructure automation. Achieved 100% success rate in deploying production-ready microservices within scheduled sprints.
